title: Sleeping in on Weekends May Be Good for Your Heart
paragraphs: Many people do not get enough sleep during the week, so they try to catch up by sleeping longer on the weekend. Some experts have warned that this habit may be bad for health. However, a new study from South Korea suggests that a little extra sleep on the weekend may actually be good for the heart.

The study was presented at the annual meeting of the European Society of Cardiology in Munich, Germany, in 2026. It was led by Dr. Lee Na-won of Korea University. The researchers used data from 40,727 adults who took part in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey between 2016 and 2023. They compared how long the participants said they slept on weekdays with how long they slept on weekends. The researchers called the difference "weekend catch-up sleep."

The results showed that weekend catch-up sleep was linked to a 6% lower chance of having high blood pressure. Among people who did not do much physical activity, the link was slightly stronger, at 7%. For these people, the lowest risk was seen among those who slept about one to two hours longer on weekends. However, when people slept even longer than that, the benefit became weaker. Among people who were physically active, there was no clear link.
High blood pressure is a major risk factor for heart attacks, strokes and other serious health problems.

Dr. Amit Green, a sleep expert who was not involved in the study, supports catching up on sleep on the weekend, but only in moderation. Green warned that sleeping four or five extra hours on the weekend could make it harder to fall asleep at the beginning of the week.

It is important to note that the study only shows a link and cannot prove that extra sleep lowers blood pressure. The participants also reported their own sleep times. In addition, the study has not yet been published in a scientific journal.
Interestingly, other research has suggested that changing sleep schedules may be bad for the heart, so more studies are needed.
